findings.summary: The estimate of the newly refused share rests on the wrong count, and that estimate is what the question to the user rests on.
findings.evidence: replay.rs:374-379 and the `ReplayRun.newly_refused` doc at 324 count a reading as newly refused only when the base build accepts it and the candidate refuses it; `total` counts every replayed case. The base build already runs `check_code_survey` (surveys.rs:199-216), so any past code or tests reading with a behavior criterion and no `Code survey:` is refused by the base and is not newly refused. Docs, design and content-only readings are untouched. The plan's figure comes from '176 of 200 commits touch crates/' (HISTORY.txt). That counts commits, not the newest 50 accepted readings that are code or tests readings with a behavior criterion and a survey the base accepts. Fix: Restate the estimate as: the share of the newest 50 accepted readings that are class code or tests, have a behavior criterion, and carry a `Code survey:` the base accepts. Label it unmeasured. Ask the user the open question with that bound, so the choice between a re-read and a run expected to be Rejected rests on the right count.

findings.summary: Making `Output:` required in every code reading adds a refusal path the request did not ask for, and the stated reason for it does not hold.
findings.evidence: The reading defines part (c) as 'an accepted record kind or a round-trip deliverable', which matters when a record is added. The plan says `Output:` is needed so 'omits exactly one of (a)-(d)' can be told apart. But the (c)-omission fixture can carry a record or data deliverable (`is_record_or_data_deliverable`, surveys.rs:140), and then (c) is required and its absence can be detected without a new label in every reading. Fix: Require (c) only when the reading has a record or data deliverable or names a new record type. Build the (c)-omission fixture with such a deliverable. Alternatively, keep `Output:` but give a correct reason for it.
findings.location: Decision 1 (`Output:` label made mandatory for every code reading)

findings.summary: The two-gate minimum is an arbitrary floor. It pushes a reader whose change has one real gate to invent a second one.
findings.evidence: The request asks the reading to state 'entry point and gate order with the stop gate'. A pure function change, such as a parser, may have the entry point as its only gate. The plan already rejects 'Allow up to two criteria per clause' as an arbitrary number, and the same objection applies here. Fix: Accept one gate identifier when it equals the stop gate, or allow 'Gate order: `<entry>` only'. Add a fixture for the one-gate case.
findings.location: Decision 6 (Gate order needs at least two distinct identifiers)

findings.summary: The plan does not say whether a clause's text includes its own label. If it does, the word 'check' in `Direct check:` satisfies the measurement-word test for every clause.
findings.evidence: Decision 1 says 'a clause runs from its label ... to the next label'. The measurement stems include `check`, and the plain word 'check' in 'Direct check' would match. Fix: State that the clause text starts after the label's colon. Add a fixture with 'Direct check: criterion 2 names `run_job`' (no measurement word) and assert it is refused.

findings.summary: The main production consumer, the live reader loop that calls `refusing_check` with the repository's files, is not named as a dependent.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:720-729 calls `refusing_check(&reading, &request.text, attempt, &referenced_jobs, Some(&repo_files))` and stores the rule name in `ReadingRefusal` (752-758). A second refusal fails the read, which is the risk the plan describes in prose. The dependents list names checks.rs and the replay callers but not this loop or its tests. Fix: Add reading.rs:720 (the reader acceptance loop and `ReadingAttempt` storage) as a dependent. Name the reader-loop tests to run (in `cargo test -p athena-core`, the reader tests that drive a fake reader through the gate).

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot with Read and Grep. The plan names real things, and they are where it says: the `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` line at checks.rs:539; `names_record_evidence`, `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, `existing_code_assumptions` and `check_code_survey` in surveys.rs (164, 237, 1329, 199); the private `clause_words` and `is_negator` in verify.rs (1368, 1378); the held-replay Blocker in verify.rs:500-512; the hold arithmetic in replay.rs:296-308 (declared share plus 5 points); `check_reading_command` in main.rs:687 with its class 'feature' fixture at 1234; the 3045-byte limit and the `< 3150` bound in briefs.rs:3591/3710, a section that includes `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`; and `INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 63]` at refusal_corpus.rs:90. Every caller of `check_reading_text` I found is a listed dependent: main.rs, drain.rs, steward.rs, replay.rs, run/tests.rs and the reading and corpus tests. The new step goes in where the fault starts, and each behavior criterion has a demonstration through production entry points with no test doubles. The plan is open that the real replay will probably hold the job (a Blocker, so the job ends Rejected) and puts that choice to the user. The accepted reading allows for this. Fixing the remaining issues would make the plan clearer or its rule narrower; none stops it from working. They are: (1) the replay-share estimate, which drives the open question, rests on the wrong count; (2) the required `Output:` label for every code reading is justified by a wrong argument; (3) a two-gate minimum in the gate order; (4) the label text may count as a measurement word; and (5) the live reader loop is not named as a dependent.
